extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for ICCV reviewers on evaluating submitted computer-vision papers, covering confidentiality, conflicts, technical evaluation, special assessment areas (reproducibility, datasets, ethics, societal impact, limitations), and review tone/quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must maintain the conference's high technical standards by evaluating papers fairly and thoroughly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate each submission with fairness and thoroughness, upholding ICCV's technical standards; ensure assessments are balanced and justified so area chairs and authors can understand the basis for decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blind review / anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: "Author Guidelines have instructed authors to make reasonable efforts to hide their identities" including names and affiliations. Reviewers should similarly maintain anonymity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to discover author identities through web searches if unknown initially. Note: arXiv preprints do not violate the anonymity policy, but reviewers must still preserve anonymity and avoid deliberate deanonymization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest check
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon assignment, verify no conflicts exist and confirm comfort reviewing each paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediately confirm you have no conflicts of interest and that you are comfortable reviewing the paper; if a conflict exists or you are uncomfortable, notify chairs so reassignment can occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical soundness and contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should demonstrate technical soundness and field contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the paper is technically correct and whether it advances the field. The guidelines encourage valuing novel approaches even when extensive benchmark testing is absent. Minor, easily corrected flaws should not by themselves justify rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuing novelty without exhaustive benchmarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Encouraged to value novel approaches even without extensive benchmark testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a submission presents a genuinely new idea or direction, weigh novelty positively even if it lacks comprehensive empirical benchmarking; consider whether limitations are addressable rather than using incomplete experiments as sole grounds for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility (optional verification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may optionally verify submitted code but aren't required to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If code is provided, reviewers can choose to run or inspect it to assess reproducibility, but there is no obligation to perform code verification as part of the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset contributions and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: If papers claim dataset contributions, public availability by camera-ready deadline is expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect datasets claimed as contributions to be made public by the camera-ready stage. Consider dataset quality, documentation, and whether release conditions are appropriate when evaluating such papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must properly cite data assets used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure datasets and other data assets are cited correctly and transparently; check for proper acknowledgement of sources and licenses where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and human-subjects considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors using personal data or human subjects require institutional review board clearance or ethical principle descriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that work involving personal data or humans includes IRB/ethics board approval where required, or at minimum a clear description of the ethical principles and protections applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Societal impact discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion encouraged but not mandatory for acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to discuss potential societal impacts of their work; reviewers may consider such discussions informative but absence of an impact discussion should not automatically disqualify a paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Honest limitation discussions should be weighted positively, not penalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors candidly describe limitations, treat that as a positive signal of rigor and transparency rather than a reason to penalize the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review specificity and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Be specific with detailed strength/weakness lists. Support recommendations thoroughly, as discussion helps authors and chairs understand your reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete examples, cite specific related work when making comparisons or claims, and avoid vague assertions. Detailed strengths/weaknesses and well-supported recommendations improve review usefulness and program committee decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vague claims (cite related work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid vague claims—cite specific publications when discussing related work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When criticizing or positioning a paper relative to prior work, reference exact papers or results rather than making unsupported general statements; this helps authors correct and contextualize contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and constructive language
rubrics_metrics.description: The tone of reviews is important — harshly written reviews will be resented by authors regardless of accuracy; word reviews constructively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use belittling, sarcastic, or overly harsh remarks. Phrase critiques constructively and respectfully, focusing on the work rather than the authors, to facilitate productive author response and community civility.
